holidays.name: Mole Day
holidays.description: Chemistry fans celebrate Avogadro's number (6.02 x 10^23) from 6:02 AM to 6:02 PM, with puns, themed parties, and plenty of cute stuffed moles.
holidays.origin: Mole Day began in the 1980s, inspired by an article in The Science Teacher by Maurice Oehler. The National Mole Day Foundation was founded in 1991 and now promotes interest in chemistry among students.
holidays.funFact: The mole in chemistry has nothing to do with the burrowing animal. The name comes from the German word 'Mol', short for 'Molekül' (molecule), though mole-themed mascots are everywhere on this day.

holidays.name: TV Talk Show Host Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate the people who keep us company with interviews, monologues, and awkward celebrity banter.
holidays.origin: This unofficial observance was created to honor talk show hosts and the role they play in pop culture. It is celebrated on October 23 and is popular among TV fans.
holidays.funFact: Late-night talk shows have been around since NBC's Tonight Starring Steve Allen in 1954, and the format has barely changed in over 70 years: desk, couch, and a band.

holidays.name: National Boston Cream Pie Day
holidays.description: Dessert lovers celebrate the Massachusetts state dessert: two layers of sponge cake filled with vanilla custard and topped with chocolate glaze. Yes, it is a cake, not a pie.
holidays.origin: The dessert is credited to chef Augustine Francois Anezin at Boston's Parker House Hotel in the 1850s. It was named a pie because cakes and pies were often baked in the same pans back then.
holidays.funFact: Boston cream pie was named the official dessert of Massachusetts in 1996, after a second-grade class pushed for it over the Toll House cookie, which also won recognition as the state cookie.

holidays.name: Swallows Return to San Juan Capistrano Day
holidays.description: A beloved California tradition celebrating the legendary annual return of cliff swallows to the historic Mission San Juan Capistrano, complete with parades and a festival.
holidays.origin: The tradition is linked to the mission's history and a famous 1939 song, 'When the Swallows Come Back to Capistrano.' The birds are traditionally said to return on March 19, but the date is also marked in the fall, when the swallows are said to depart on October 23.
holidays.funFact: Swallows migrate thousands of miles to Argentina each year. In recent years, fewer swallows have been nesting at the mission itself, partly because of the restoration of the old stone church.

holidays.name: Slap Your Annoying Coworker Day (Unofficial Joke Observance)
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek office holiday where you imagine sending annoying coworkers a good-natured wake-up call. Everyone is encouraged to leave the actual slapping to the imagination and keep HR happy.
holidays.origin: A satirical observance that spread through internet holiday calendars and office humor. It is not an official holiday, and is generally celebrated by sharing jokes about workplace pet peeves.
holidays.funFact: Surveys regularly show that loud chewing, reply-all emails, and microwaved fish top the list of office pet peeves.
